decisions.summary: Candidates counted at the registry's Standing.admits/conflicts. A stage's own candidate loop is counted only when it is rebuilt (444 box 5). Until then each unrebuilt stage's count is recorded as 'a lower bound'.
decisions.why: FR-001 and request section 1 put counters 'at each stage's candidate loop' in this feature. Request section 6 step 1 is 'the counters, make work-budget and today's figures for every stage', and checklist box 4 (today's measurement, ratio to budget) comes before box 5 (rebuild). Counters that arrive at box 5 undercount the very measurement the ratio is built from. The plan concedes this ('its count is a lower bound'). The request's purpose is to show how far each stage is from its budget ('nothing showed that the roll does 100-200x too much work'), and a figure that can only understate that distance works against it. Nothing makes the literal reading impossible: each loop takes the same one-line increment D1 already uses. Cost does not count. Fix: T01 puts the one-line 'candidate' increment in every stage's candidate loop now, listing the loops with the command that produced the list. Alternatively, the plan records a measurement that every stage's candidates pass through Standing.admits, so that admits IS each stage's candidate counter, and drops the lower-bound clause for the candidate count. Not counting inline arithmetic outside the three FR-001 sites is within and is not part of this ruling.

decisions.summary: budget-set's only stated refusal is a verdict that does not read SOUND. It has no condition on the stage's current status.
decisions.why: Request section 5.4: 'Budgets change only with the GM's words.' FR-005: a FIRST budget needs SOUND; 'a raise needs make budget-change with the GM's words'. As written, budget-set can be run again on a budgeted or accepted stage with a fresh SOUND verdict and a higher PER_THING or EXPONENT, which raises a budget with no GM words and no log row. That gives the 'one writer' a second route past the guard. Fix: budget-set refuses unless the stage's status is 'unbudgeted', naming make budget-change. Any change to an existing budget goes through budget-change.

The plan's counters are keyed by kind and attributed by stage only, so the bundle cannot carry counts by function. Reading 'by function' as 'by stage' would complete the GM's thought. The cost to the purpose is concrete: OVER must name the chain, and per-stage totals by kind cannot locate one. The fix adds to FR-002 without contradicting it: stage attribution stays, and each counting site also keys the function it sits in, in the same one-line, call-free form (D1). decisions.summary: The inventory check scans only files under scripts/ and l7r/diagram/tools/, plus Makefile recipes matched by tool name (ruff, pyrefly, pytest, coverage, testmon, vulture).
decisions.why: Request section 7: the check 'lists every hook, gate script and make target that reads .py files or Python's syntax tree', with the stated purpose 'A new Python-only check therefore cannot be added without saying what happens to it under Rust'. The GM's 2026-10-28 words ask that tooling enforcing conventions mechanically 'not be forgotten or lost'. The plan limits the census to two directories and gives no measurement that every such reader lives there. Request section 7's own table names readers the plan never places inside the bound: the cache's engine hash (gencache.engine_files()), the STAGES/Steps: docstring reader for the placement-stages page, and the claims and make tunables reader. Any reader added outside the two directories, and any convention test that parses .py, escapes, which is the purpose's exact failure. Matching Makefile recipes by tool name alone also misses a recipe that reads .py inline (find -name '*.py', python -c with ast). Fix: scan every tracked file (git ls-files), or state each excluded directory with a census command showing it holds no reader. Apply the plan's own .py-reader patterns to Makefile recipe text as well as the tool names.

decisions.summary: Every stage's candidate loops are taken to be 'the anchors make perf-fanout names per stage at 40 households', recorded in research/candidate-loops.md.
decisions.why: The GM: counters 'at each phase's candidate loop'. The design itself describes perf-fanout's output as 'the hot chains' (checklist box 4), which is a selection by call volume, and the plan does not show that perf-fanout names every loop. As written the search space is 'loops that anchor a hot chain', not 'every loop that tries candidates', so a candidate loop with little call volume is left uncounted. That defeats the purpose: candidates per thing placed is the S2 factor every budget is built on, and step 1 asks for today's figures for every stage. Fix: build the census by walking each stage's code for every loop that tries a site (submits it to Standing.admits/conflicts or tests it against the _geom layer), and state that search space and its command in research/candidate-loops.md. perf-fanout's anchors then serve as a cross-check that the walk missed nothing, not as the source.

decisions.summary: A stage none of whose anchors is a candidate loop records that it has none ('the seat, the sink').
decisions.why: A stage that truly has no candidate loop has nothing to count, so recording 'none' would be legitimate. But the trigger as written is the anchor list (a sample of hot chains), not the stage's code, so a stage with a cool candidate loop is recorded as having none while it tries candidates. Also, '(the seat, the sink)' names the result before the walk runs, a premise nobody measured. Legitimate once it rests on the code walk in D2-loops-census, with the examples removed or marked as expectations pending that walk.

decisions.summary: Inline arithmetic outside the named sites is not counted in unrebuilt stages; Python calls are printed beside the counts; a rebuilt phase counts every inner loop and MODE AUDIT rules UNCOUNTED otherwise.
decisions.why: The design names where the counters live and records Python calls 'beside these figures'. S5 binds a rebuilt phase and the plan keeps it binding, through box 5 and MODE AUDIT.

decisions.summary: T01 holds only D1, D3 and D2's shared sites (primitives, indexes, registry); each stage family's candidate-loop counters move to T09-T12, each its own landing, T01 first
decisions.why: D2 lists both the shared sites and the candidate loops; dividing them among tasks drops neither, and the order (T01's module before the increments that use it) is forced by D1.

decisions.summary: The candidate-loop walk is partitioned into four families naming 23 stages (T09: water_frame, field, sink, waterward, pond_stock, pond_bank; T10: seat, homesteads, appurtenances, burial, lane_wells, sties, washing; T11: track, web, crossings; T12: hinterland, woodland, windbreak, bamboo, frame, notice, labels)
decisions.why: D2 requires every stage's candidate loops, walked from STAGES; the request says about 25 stages. The blocks enumerate 23 with no statement that the four lists are STAGES entire and no command or date that produced them, so a stage absent from every family would go unwalked - its candidates uncounted and its 'none' never decided by the walk, which D2 forbids. An enumeration with no search space cannot be checked, and an exception is presumed wrong. Fix: the Task approaches block (or each family header) names the command and date that listed STAGES and states that the four lists are that set entire, every stage in exactly one family; a stage outside them gets a family.

decisions.summary: Each family starts from the scan's loops in research/candidate-loops.md, filtered by hand, with named hand-reads where the scan cannot reach (getattr-dispatched _seat_region/_free_ground/_access/_site_corridors, homesteads/stages.py, water/brook*.py, water/polder.py, hinterland/parcels/*, groves, labels/*, and the fanout cross-check's misses in gap_ways.py and meet.py); filtered list and excluded loops written with why
decisions.why: D2 makes the walk the source and the fanout a cross-check; the scan is the walk's recorded first pass, the hand-reads extend it past what a static scan misses, the filter is D2's own criterion (a loop that tries a site), and recording each exclusion with its reason keeps the search space checkable.

decisions.summary: T11 sorts the ~350 scanned ways/ loops into trials (counted) and measurements (excluded)
decisions.why: D2 counts a candidate per site tried; a measuring loop's _geom calls are already counted at the shared sites. Same decision at any loop count. Note: '~350' carries no m: key or dated label in the block; it should point at the scan's date or the research file's command line.

decisions.summary: n = 1 per iteration; len(cands) before a comprehension, sorted or min over a list; a short-circuiting next/first-admitted search counted inside the predicate it calls, keyed with that predicate
decisions.why: Matches D1 (key names the kind and the function the increment sits in, n the element count of a whole-list operation) and D2 (one candidate per candidate tried): exhaustive operations touch every element, a short-circuit search only those it tries.

decisions.summary: Green exit: every listed loop counted, calls unmoved within one in a thousand, make cohort-landing unregressed; done when the family's research section is complete and its counts print per stage
decisions.why: The call tolerance is SC-001's; cohort-landing enforces the request's 'engine counters only; no map changes'; the completed research section is D2's record.

decisions.why: Each enforces a stated requirement (SC-001, FR-004's inertness, FR-001's correctness); the request records Python calls and times beside the counts without making them targets, and the A/B is a record, not a gate.

decisions.summary: The source is an ast call graph over hamletgen, settlement, waterfields, sitegen, overlap and labels. It follows resolved calls (an import, self., a module attribute, a unique method name) and lists every loop, comprehension and min/max/sorted/next in a reached function whose subtree calls a test, directly or through a testing helper. A getattr dispatch, a module reached only by name matching, the modules on the 'not fully walked' list, and water/brook*.py and water/polder.py are read by hand.
decisions.why: The stated reach follows CALLS only. A function passed BY REFERENCE is a Name or Attribute node, not a Call: min(cands, key=self._gap), sorted(..., key=f), filter(ok, cands), map(f, cands) or a callback. So a bare key-function min or sorted, or a filter or map over a testing predicate, has no test call in its subtree and is not listed. The plan knows the form exists, because its own counter rule names 'a key function' as a counting site. But the reach does not say references are resolved, and the hand-read list does not name them. filter and map are not among the listed forms at all. A second, lesser gap: a method call whose name is NOT unique is unresolved under the stated rule, and the text does not say whether that falls inside 'not fully walked' or is dropped. The fanout cross-check does not cure this. D2 makes the walk the source and allows a stage 'none' only by the walk (this block's step 2 says the same), so a stage whose only candidate loop is a key-function min would be written 'none' by the source. This is not impossible to cover, it is not implied by the request, and it defeats D2's walk-as-source. The fix is to state that function-valued arguments (key=, filter, map, callbacks) are resolved as reaches and filter and map are listed forms, or else to name them in the hand-read residue, and to say where unresolved non-unique method calls go.

decisions.summary: n = 1 per iteration. Where the test is a named predicate or a key function, the inline increment goes inside it, keyed with it, with no call.
decisions.why: This is FR-001 literally: an inline increment inside if __debug__ with no call, once per candidate (request.md: 'count once per element').

decisions.summary: Only a bare sorted or min, or an inline lambda over a list, takes OPS[...] += len(cands) before it.
decisions.why: This is an exception to FR-001's 'no function call'. It is implied by FR-001's own clause 'a vectorized operation counts its elements' and by the GM's 'They count once per element, even when a vectorized call handles many elements' (request.md section 1). A bare sorted or min over a list is a C-level operation over n elements with no Python body to hold an increment, which is exactly that case. A lambda cannot hold a statement. The exception is scoped to those forms only, and any named predicate or key function counts inside itself. FR-001's stated purpose also still holds, because a C builtin raises no sys.monitoring PY_START event, and the exit re-measures the calls. The ruling does not rest on the figure '7,564,885 calls in both engines'. That figure points only at research/overhead.md and carries no m: key and no date, so it fails the figures rule on its face. Give it an m: key or a dated method label.

decisions.summary: A loop whose only test is the registry's admits or conflicts takes no candidate@<function> counter of its own. It is counted by the registry's candidate@Standing.conflicts.
decisions.why: This is NEW since the last verdict, and it is a direct narrowing of D2's 'each gets a candidate@<function> increment per candidate tried'. D2's registry bullet already counts a candidate on every admits or conflicts call. So a loop counter on a loop whose only test is the registry would count the same candidate twice, against the GM's 'count once per element' (request.md section 1). That resolves D2's two bullets in favor of the GM's words. The carve-out is tight: a loop that also tests against _geom keeps its own counter. What it costs is which function the candidates came from inside a stage. FR-002's per-stage attribution and step 1's per-stage figures do not need that.

decisions.summary: Green requires the Python calls unmoved within SC-001's one in a thousand, read from make perf-fanout's Python functions as research/overhead.md reads them.
decisions.why: SC-001 measures 'the Python calls make perf-fanout counts'. The request defines Python call counts as the thing that misses work in C, including builtins ('They also miss work done in C: shapely, numpy and builtins', request.md section 1). So reading Python functions only is SC-001's own measure, and not a reading chosen to hide the len() calls.
